items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-07-23, 08-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Daniel Raposo. He died. Yeah. Anyway, uh, the, uh, I was always wondering about the salary with the Basin Street Six...

ctx.x: Whatever happened to the clarinet player? What's his name now? I don't know.

Daniel Raposo. He died. Yeah. Anyway, uh, the, uh, I was always wondering about the salary with the Basin Street Six, how the financial arrangements were, who the lead it was, how the all that arranged things.

It was, uh, I went on the Basin Street Six, and it was a terrific salary at that time. I was making a hundred dollars a week. It's 1953, huh? 52, 53, I guess. When, uh, when, uh, scale, when musicians was only about fifty-eight dollars a week, fifty-six dollars a week. And I was the lowest paid dialing band. I was not one of the, uh, cooperative owners. The rest of the band was, it was a cooperative band. And, uh, it was kind of, uh, how can you say, whoever hollered the loudest got the tone played he wanted. But…
